text:
Matvei Michkov did not play Friday, and in Philadelphia that will be the story until he plays again. The Flyers scratched him against Vancouver, teammates learned of it the same day, and Rick Tocchet said afterward, per Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports, that Michkov will be in the lineup Saturday. The Flyers won without him. Meanwhile Travis Konecny's name keeps turning up in trade reports, and Daniel Briere has reportedly told callers Michkov is not available.

All of that sits on top of a team that is better than it was a month ago. Philadelphia is 6-2-2 over its last ten, winning 54% of the expected goals in that stretch, after a 10-12-6 start overall. Noah Cates has scored late winners, and his line with Michkov and rookie Porter Martone has 62% of the expected goals. Denver Barkey has earned Tocchet's praise at center.

The season numbers are still sobering: 46.7% of the expected goals and 44% at five on five, near the bottom of the league. And neither goalie is helping right now. Dan Vladar is .857 over his last five starts and Joseph Woll .860, a combined 7.5 goals worse than expected. Trevor Zegras has 1 point in his last 10 games on 6.4 expected, which is more bad luck than bad play.

Our numbers give the Flyers a 12% chance at the playoffs. What we'd watch: whether the Michkov situation settles quietly, because the line he anchors is the best thing Philadelphia has.
